methods.notes: Match any known name or FF20; some shorter advertisement samples omit FF20.

identification.notes: Match a known name or FF20, then confirm the GATT layout. The observed 0x1812/company-0x05D6 advertisement is corroboration only: 0x1812 is the shared HID service and the company/prefix combination has one captured unit behind it, so neither is declared as an independent matcher.

device.name: SPOTLED LED Panel
device.notes:
OEM full-colour LED matrix panels driven by SPOTLED (Android package com.led.spotled; iOS bundleId com.sunday.led, App Store id 1564039607). SPOTLED 1.9.4 (2023) is the last release on both platforms. The same protocol covers hats, badges, backpack skins, chest panels and flexible banners under many reseller names. Lunchbox / LEDs 2 RAVE 4 Dream Skin 2.0 and early 3.0 panels are members; leds2rave4-lunchbox-led.yaml carries the retail generations. THIS spec is the canonical protocol reference.
DISCOVERY: reseller-set names vary. Known prefixes are LBXDRMSKIN_LED_ and SpotLED_. FF20 is useful when advertised but can be absent from short advertisements. The tested panel advertises 0x1812 and manufacturer company 0x05D6; neither is a family-wide unique matcher, so do not match generic HID-over-GATT devices on 0x1812 alone. Confirm FF20/FF21/FF22 after connect.
PAIRING IS OPTIONAL, NOT ABSENT: bondless community clients work. The official app initiates legacy Just Works pairing; the captured panel answers No Bonding, distributes no LTK, and the phone requests encryption for that connection. There is no PIN, MITM protection or persistent bond requirement.
BOOTSTRAP: connect, negotiate MTU, enable FF21 notifications through the GATT client, discover FF21/FF22, then query Version, DisplayInfo and BufferSize, awaiting each FF21 notification. The official app's fuller order is version -> display -> animation/text capability -> playlist/object queries -> receive capacity. The three queries in this spec are sufficient for the documented upload path; do not treat notification values as ATT characteristic reads. Use the standard two-byte 01 00 CCCD value if writing the descriptor directly, and never write descriptor bytes to FF21 itself.
LEGACY COMMAND FRAME (FF21): [u8 frame_length][u8 command_id] [u16_be serial][u16_be command_type][u32_be command_length]. Fixed queries are only the first four bytes. Vendor serial counters are byte-wide and wrap at 255 although the wire fields are wider; other clients use the full fields.
LEGACY DATA FRAME (FF22): 15-byte header [u32_be header_length=15] [u16_be command_type=0x8004][u32_be serial][u32_be content_length] [u8 checksum], then typed records [u32_be length][u16_be type][fields] [u8 checksum]. Record types: 2 colour, 3 character, 4 character string, 5 word stock, 6 lattice frame, 7 time, 8 effect, 9 speed, 10 number bar, 11 animation, 13 font glyph, 14 brightness (0-100), 15 screen mode (0 normal / 1 upside-down / 2 mirror / 3 both), 96 dynamic colour frame. Effects: 0 none, 1 up, 2 down, 3 left, 4 right, 5 stack, 6 expand, 7 laser. Checksum: sum the covered bytes; when the sum exceeds 0xFF negate it with (~sum)+1 and keep the low byte. Preserve the conditional: a sum already below 0x100 is emitted unchanged.
UPLOAD FLOW CONTROL: send SendingDataStart and require type-2 status zero with matching serial and command type. Serialize the complete data payload once, then slice it into raw writes; never add a length/checksum to each ATT chunk. The official app uses 182-byte application chunks in the captured legacy session even after MTU 512 was negotiated; MTU-3 is a ceiling, not a promise of the app's chosen size. Pace writes and react to responses. ContinueSending (type 255) has no status byte: it carries the command type at bytes 4-5 and the offset to RESUME FROM at bytes 6-9, not the client's cursor. The capture paused after exactly 7280 bytes and resumed both 13902-byte transfers successfully. Finish with SendingDataFinish and require type-4 status zero with matching serial and command type. PauseSending (type 254) is not by itself an MTU diagnosis.
TEXT: rendering client-side into animation/type-96 frames is the capture- proven route. Character-string records let the device lay out text but need font/glyph records first. The tested firmware reported a 160-character UI limit; older community clients used smaller conservative limits.
FIRMWARE AND NEWER APPS: static analysis now identifies the FF10 OTA service, FF11 instructions, FF12 data, and the metadata download flow; the OTA wire sequence remains reported, not capture-verified. PIXELY GLOW keeps the legacy FF20 transport on this panel and also contains protocol v2/v3 paths. Those extensions are recorded separately below and must not be sent merely because a panel speaks the captured legacy protocol.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app or other central; power-cycle the panel if it no longer advertises or accept connections.

pairing.notes: Bondless operation is confirmed. In the 2026-11-10 SMP capture the app asks for bonding/MITM/Secure Connections, but the panel selects legacy Just Works, No Bonding, no MITM and no LTK distribution. The phone then enables encryption for the connection. Do not describe this as a secure persistent bond or as proof that pairing never occurs.

credentials.notes: Physical proximity is the only established access control. Transient pairing does not provide MITM protection or a durable owner credential.

factory_reset.effect: No factory wipe is established. Power-cycling drops the current connection; it is not evidence that user content or settings are erased.

procedures.basis: Observed connection recovery during owner testing; no factory-reset operation was found or exercised.
procedures.name: Power cycle (connection recovery only)

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection; stored content is not claimed to be cleared.

methods.description: Power on, scan, connect and enable FF21 notifications. This project completed queries and uploads without a persistent bond. A transient official-app Just Works exchange is optional, not a provisioning step.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect, enable FF21 notifications, then issue the Version, DisplayInfo and BufferSize queries and await their notifications.

setup.notes: No provisioning, account or network credential exchange. Pairing is not required for control; an official-app pairing attempt may still occur.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the panel to a network or owner. Rediscover and connect from the new controller, closing the old central first. No persistent LTK bond was established in the official-app capture.

testing.notes: This project queried and uploaded to a 96x16 RGB Lunchbox panel on 2026-11-07/08. A supplied 2026-11-10 official-app Pixel 8 capture of the same panel generation independently confirmed all queries, seven data transactions, one- and three-frame RGB888 uploads, visual RGB channel order, and offset resume after exactly 7280 data bytes. The official-app capture was analysed, not generated by our client; OTA, PIXELY protocol v2/v3, other geometries, monochrome panels and settings writes remain unverified.

variants.notes: See leds2rave4-lunchbox-led.yaml for SP107E v1 and recent iLEDColor v3, which are different protocols.

entities.name: LED Panel
entities.notes: Brightness is a type-14 FF22 data record; no generic state decoder or verified brightness write is declared.

entities.name: Screen Mode
entities.notes: Screen mode is a three-byte type-15 FF22 record (value plus two padding bytes); writes remain unverified.

features.notes: The official-app capture contains one- and three-frame 96x16 RGB888 DynamicColorFrame uploads; decoded frames match camera images, including RGB order. Each frame record is 4620 bytes. Three-frame 13902-byte transfers pause at 7280 bytes, resume from that offset, and finish with matching type-4 acknowledgements. This proves three frames, not the advertised 20-frame limit or arbitrary geometry. Earlier custom-client three/eight-frame attempts failed; their serialization difference remains unresolved.

dfu_mode.notes: No separate bootloader advertisement, name or address is established.

enter.notes: Sequence: query ready -> query ACK window -> stream command-82 image blocks -> query complete. No OTA capture was made.

image.format: Raw .bin image; whole-image CRC-16 (poly 0x1021, init 0, MSB-first) and u24 length are presented before transfer.
image.notes: Firmware metadata is recovered from the vendor API and images exist, but signature enforcement and exact hardware compatibility are not established. CRC is an integrity check, not proof of authorization.

dfu.notes: FF10/FF11/FF12 and the command sequence come from static app analysis. Do not replay an image from this documentary block alone.

advertisement.protocol_selection: PIXELY GLOW reads a big-endian u16 protocol value from a seven-byte manufacturer AD structure and selects protocol 3 at >= 0x0300; this captured value selects legacy behavior.
advertisement.scope: One 96x16 legacy panel; not a universal family signature and not an independent matcher.

container.checksum: Same conditional byte-sum/two's-complement rule as the data header and other records
container.content_length_formula: 9 + frame_count * dynamic_frame_bytes + 10 + 8; the 15-byte data header is additional
container.record_envelope: u32_be record length at 0, u16_be type at 4, fields at 6, then one checksum byte at the end; length includes the complete record

bitmap.rgb888_order: R,G,B per pixel, left to right then top to bottom

synthetic_three_frame_vector.note: Three solid primary-color frames invented for this vector; no captured user image is included

time_type.note: Raw type; only zero is captured

colour_types.note: Only RGB888/type-96 on a 96x16 panel is capture-confirmed; the other modes are static app findings.

continue_layout.matching_rule: Require response type 255 and the request's serial and command type. This reply has no status byte; do not apply query_layout or transfer_ack_layout.

pause_recovery_code.note: Static app finding only; nonzero aborts the transfer. No PauseSending reply was captured.

flow_control.rule: For ContinueSending, match response type, serial and command type, resume from the device offset, and deduplicate retransmitted ATT chunks. Do not read a status byte from type 255. Start and finish replies separately require status zero at byte 4.

transfer_ack_layout.matching_rule: Require response type 2 or 4 as applicable, status zero, and the request's serial and command type.

metadata_endpoint.note: The metadata endpoint was exercised without authentication in research; image host configuration and exact model selection still need care.
metadata_endpoint.request: Device JSON with protocolVersion forced to zero

pixely_glow_extensions.boundary: Static findings from PIXELY GLOW 1.0.4/1.9.9; not observed on the captured legacy panel and not a license to probe every SPOTLED unit.

protocol_3.checksum: Same conditional byte-sum/two's-complement rule as legacy data records.
protocol_3.response_layout: Request/response ID at bytes 4-5, serial at 7-8, status at 9, payload from 12 where applicable.
protocol_3.transport: Large writes are MTU-chunked and matched by serial/status, not the legacy ContinueSending receive-window mechanism.

protocol_query.value: u32 big-endian; >= 0x0200 selects aggregate device-info object 0xFFFF

remaining_unknowns: Earlier custom-client three/eight-frame RGB uploads failed although the official three-frame path succeeds. Identify the byte-level difference before blaming a panel resource limit; the advertised 20-frame field is still not a proven guarantee.
Other geometries, monochrome/RGB332/RGB565 modes, arbitrary animations, device-rendered text, brightness/screen-mode writes, factory reset and OTA remain unverified by a live client.
FF10 OTA framing is source-derived only; image signature policy, recovery and model compatibility are unknown. AE30 remains unexplained.
PIXELY GLOW protocol v2/v3, aggregate device info, material shapes/borders and protocol-3 uploads need advertisement-gated hardware captures; none are claimed for this legacy unit.

get_animation_text_capability.description: Query animation/text capability (command 26, response 27). Newer firmware may append a u32 storage size.

get_buffer_size.description: Query the u32 big-endian receive window; full notification is 9 bytes.

get_display_info.description: Query dimensions, colour type, advertised frame limit, brightness and font count; full base notification is 13 bytes.

get_version.description: Query hardware type/revision and firmware revision; full base notification is 15 bytes.

sending_data_finish.description: Finish a data payload; require response type 4, not type 2, with status zero and matching serial and command type. The acknowledgement carries status at byte 4 and command type at bytes 5-6.

sending_data_start.description: Announce a data payload; require response type 2 with status zero and matching serial and command type. The acknowledgement carries status at byte 4 and command type at bytes 5-6.

characteristics.name: Command
characteristics.notes: Values/templates below are COMPLETE legacy frames; do not prepend another length or append a checksum. The command channel has no checksum. Notification layout and field offsets are declared under protocol_details.legacy_responses. A notification can contain a complete response rather than an ATT read-back value.

characteristics.name: Data
characteristics.notes: Bulk legacy data channel. The 15-byte payload header and each typed record carry their own length/checksum; individual ATT writes do not. Slice the serialized stream into writes no larger than MTU-3. The captured official app chose 182-byte writes at negotiated MTU 512. ContinueSending offset resume is mandatory after a receive-window pause. Brightness and screen mode are data records, not FF21 commands.

initialization.notes: Enable notifications through the GATT client; the captured CCCD value is the standard 01 00.
Version first in the official bootstrap; await type 17.
Await type-19 DisplayInfo and use its geometry rather than a retail-model assumption.
Await type-21 receive-capacity/BufferSize notification before uploads.

ota_query_ack_window.advanced_reason: Part of the firmware-update sequence; do not issue outside an owner-approved update.
ota_query_ack_window.description: Query the device's OTA acknowledgement window before sending image data.

ota_query_complete.advanced_reason: Finalizes a firmware update; only use after every image block and acknowledgement completed.
ota_query_complete.description: Ask whether the streamed image is complete; response status zero means done.

ota_query_ready.advanced_reason: Starts a firmware-update session. Use only an exact-model vendor image and preserve power; no recovery path has been tested.
ota_query_ready.description: Begin OTA by presenting whole-image CRC-16 and length; expect readiness before streaming.

crc_hi.description: High byte of CRC-16 poly 0x1021, init 0, MSB-first over the complete image.

crc_lo.description: Low byte of the same CRC.

len_b0.description: Least-significant byte of the image length.

len_b2.description: Most-significant byte of the u24 big-endian image length.

characteristics.name: OTA Data
characteristics.notes: Command 82 (0x52) carries image bytes in application blocks; wait for an acknowledgement at each device-supplied window. Static analysis reports five application-MTU units per block and 20 ms pacing, but no capture validates those values or image compatibility.

services.name: SPOTLED OTA Service
services.notes: Enumerated on the tested unit and identified in two app generations. Ordinary display traffic stays on FF20. The OTA command IDs use a little-endian 16-bit ID field, unlike the legacy display command IDs.
